style.vernacular: Capital of Equatorial Guinea on the north of volcanic Bioko island, wet (about 1,850 mm a year) and hazy under rainforest-covered slopes. The old centre keeps Spanish colonial buildings (1890s-1950s): rendered masonry and a few weathered 19th-century timber houses in white, pale blue and ochre, a Neo-Gothic cathedral with two 40 m towers, a square street grid, low skyline and many green spaces. Since the oil boom of the 1990s-2000s the outskirts are filled with white or pastel painted concrete blocks, glass-fronted banks, big stadiums and gated villas under red-brown or blue corrugated roofs. Streets are paved; roadsides are red-brown volcanic earth with palms and broadleaf trees. Colours are typical Gulf of Guinea palettes, not individually sourced.
style.ornament: Neo-Gothic pointed arches and rose windows on the cathedral; colonial verandas with turned timber balusters and wooden louvre shutters on old houses; Spanish-style tiled eaves and pastel stucco; modern government buildings with flag poles, white columns and presidential-style gates.

sources.what: Spanish colonial architecture coexists with modern post-independence buildings; 19th-century wooden buildings on Nigeria and Rey Boncoro streets; Cathedral of Santa Isabel (1897-1916); Presidential and Justice palaces; Casa Teodolita 1902; National Library 1916; square street grid, low buildings, green areas; airport, port and 2007 stadium are modern
tropical monsoon climate ~1,850 mm rain, wet March-November, fog and haze; 19th-century wooden buildings; renewed airport; Estadio de Malabo built 2007
island mostly covered by tropical rainforest; volcanic basalt; Pico Basile 3,012 m; Krio planters' cocoa farms
